questions.template: What is the tens digit of {n}?
questions.hint: The tens digit is the one on the LEFT in a two-digit number.
questions.explain: In {n}, the left digit counts the tens — so it's {answer}.

questions.template: What is the ones digit of {n}?
questions.hint: The ones digit sits at the very END of the number.
questions.explain: In {n}, the last digit counts the ones — that's {answer}.

questions.template: {a} tens and {b} ones make which number?
questions.hint: Tens are worth ten each — {a} tens is {a}0.
Only the tens digit changes when you add ten.

questions.template: What is the hundreds digit of {n}?
questions.hint: The hundreds digit is the FIRST of the three digits.
questions.explain: In {n}, the first digit counts hundreds — it's {answer}.

questions.template: What is the VALUE of the hundreds digit in {n}?
questions.hint: The digit tells you HOW MANY hundreds — so multiply it by 100.
questions.explain: The hundreds digit of {n} is worth that many hundreds: {answer}.

questions.template: {a} hundreds, {b} tens and {c} ones make which number?
questions.hint: Write them in order: hundreds, then tens, then ones.
questions.explain: {a} hundreds is {a}00, {b} tens is {b}0, plus {c} — together {answer}.

questions.template: What is the thousands digit of {n}?
questions.hint: Four digits: the FIRST one counts thousands.
questions.explain: In {n} the first digit counts thousands — it's {answer}.

questions.template: What is the VALUE of the tens digit in {n}?
questions.hint: Find the tens digit first, then remember each ten is worth 10.
questions.explain: The tens digit of {n} is worth {answer}.

questions.hint: Only the thousands digit grows by one.
Look at the tens digit: 5 or more rounds UP.
questions.explain: {n} sits closest to {answer} on the number line.
